terms.gloss: a pyramid, the solid and the Egyptian monument
terms.comment: A Greek loan with its long ȳ (Greek πυραμίς). Cicero names it among the solid figures beside the cone and the cylinder; Gellius gives the Greek accusative plural pȳramidas.

terms.gloss: a three-sided cone: Gellius’s Latin for a pyramid
terms.comment: Gellius’s description: a mēta is the cone-shaped turning post of the Circus (see “cone”).

phrases.latin: Ex cubīs pȳramidem exstruāmus: īnfimō ōrdine novem, deinde quattuor, summō ūnum.
phrases.english: Let’s build a pyramid out of the blocks: nine in the bottom row, then four, one on top.

phrases.latin: At mihi vel cylindrī vel quadrātī vel cōnī vel pȳramidis vidētur esse fōrmōsior.
phrases.english: But to me the shape of a cylinder, or a cube, or a cone, or a pyramid seems more beautiful.

phrases.latin: quālēs sunt fermē mētae triangulae, quās “pȳramidas” appellant
phrases.english: such as are, roughly, three-sided cones, which they call “pyramids”

sources: Lewis & Short: pyramis · Lewis & Short: meta
